Environment Setup — VS Code & GitHub

Week 1 · Day 1  |  Tools Installation & Configuration
🔵

Visual Studio Code — Installation

Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is a free, open-source code editor by Microsoft. It supports all major programming languages, has a rich extension ecosystem, and is the industry-standard editor for web development. We downloaded and installed it as our primary development environment for this internship.

1

Download VS Code

Visited code.visualstudio.com and clicked the Download for Windows button to download the installer.

2

Accept License Agreement

Ran the installer, selected "I accept the agreement" on the License screen, then clicked Next to proceed.

[] 3

Review Additional Tasks & Install

Confirmed additional tasks (Add to PATH, context menu options) and clicked Install to begin extraction.

4

Installation in Progress

The setup wizard extracted all VS Code files to C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code. Progress bar filled to completion.

5

VS Code Ready!

VS Code launched to the Welcome screen. Recent projects, walkthroughs, and Python Development guides were visible and accessible.

✅

Result: VS Code was successfully installed and launched. The Python extension was already available from a prior setup. The editor is now ready for all Week 1 coding tasks.

🟢

GitHub Desktop — Setup & Repository Creation

GitHub is a cloud-based platform for version control and collaboration using Git. GitHub Desktop provides a graphical interface for managing repositories, committing code, and pushing changes — without needing command-line expertise. We installed GitHub Desktop, signed in with our GitHub account, and created our first repository.

1

Download GitHub Desktop

Visited desktop.github.com and clicked Download for Windows (64bit) to get the installer.

2

Welcome Screen — Sign In

After installation, GitHub Desktop opened its welcome screen. Clicked Sign in to GitHub.com to authenticate via browser.

3

Enter GitHub Credentials

Browser opened the GitHub login page. Entered username/email and password, then clicked the green Sign in button.

4

Configure Git Identity

GitHub Desktop showed the Configure Git screen. Selected Use my GitHub account name and email, confirmed the details, and clicked Finish.

5

GitHub Dashboard — Signed In

Successfully authenticated. The GitHub dashboard showed all existing repositories under the account saisalpure5-ops.

6

Create New Repository

Navigated to github.com/new to create a new repository. Filled in the repository name, set visibility to Public, and submitted.

✅

Result: GitHub Desktop was installed, authenticated with the account saisalpure5-ops, and Git was configured with the correct identity. The internship project folder TL_Intern_Sai is now tracked and ready for version control throughout all 4 weeks.
